classification.difficultyReason: Translate equal-side and perimeter relationships into two simultaneous equations and interpret both unknown lengths.

content.prompt:
Solve by introducing two pronumerals and forming two simultaneous equations, even though the problem may be done more easily using one pronumeral.

The equal sides of an isosceles triangle are 5 cm longer than the base. If the perimeter of the triangle is 34 cm, find the side lengths of the triangle.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ cm be the base length and $y$ cm be the length of each equal side.

$$\begin{align*}y&=x+5 &&(1)\\x+2y&=34 &&(2)\end{align*}$$

Substitute equation (1) into equation (2).

$$\begin{align*}x+2(x+5)&=34\\3x+10&=34\\3x&=24\\x&=8\end{align*}$$

Substitute $x=8$ into equation (1).

$$\begin{align*}y&=8+5\\y&=13\end{align*}$$

The side lengths are 8 cm, 13 cm and 13 cm.

Check: $13-8=5$ and $8+13+13=34$.
